items.fullText: U.S. news Waymo robotaxis banned from California freeways The ban was imposed after a pair of incidents near San Francisco, state officials said. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 A Waymo robotaxi drives in North Beach in San Francisco. Heather Diehl / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 17, 2026, 6:24 PM EST By Tim Stelloh and Lindsay Good California banned Waymo robotaxis from state freeways after officials determined that the driverless vehicles pose an “imminent hazard to public safety,” the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday. In a news release, the department said it had issued the Nov. 11 ban after one of the company’s autonomous vehicles tried to pass highway patrol officers conducting a traffic break on a San Francisco-area freeway this month. The department also cited a separate incident in which three of the company’s vehicles entered an active construction closure on another San Francisco-area highway. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” the department said. Similar restrictions were placed on the company after similar incidents earlier this year, the department said. The ban will remain in place until Waymo can address the issue, according to the release. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: Artificial intelligence U.S. closes loophole that let Chinese companies use top AI chips through foreign data centers The Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday morning that it would clamp down on the sale of chips to data center customers in Southeast Asian countries. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced questions in recent months about why the department's Entity List had not been updated for over a year. Alex Brandon / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:44 PM EST / Updated Nov. 17, 2026, 8:20 AM EST By Jared Perlo The Commerce Department moved to further restrict the sale of top-tier American AI chips Monday morning, addressing mounting concerns about how companies in China and other countries might evade American export restrictions by taking advantage of longstanding loopholes. As part of a new rule, data center customers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil must now receive a special license from the Commerce Department in order to buy advanced AI chips from American companies such as Nvidia or AMD. Over the past several years, businesses in those countries have bought billions of dollars worth’ of high-end chips, raising concerns that some chips might be illegally smuggled into China. The rule, issued by the department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, will also require existing overseas data center customers to receive a similar license if they provide “significant volumes” of computing power to companies whose headquarters are in China, Russia, Cuba or other countries banned from receiving certain types of advanced American technology. Companies in these countries have allowed Chinese businesses to access their most advanced AI chips remotely , skirting rules that prevented Chinese companies from accessing these chips on Chinese territory. items.d: Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors.  Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows […]
items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w

items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean. items.fullText: AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner Health systems and startups are using the latest AI technologies to support clinicians, streamline workflows and improve patient care. November 13, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients. Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI outputs and guiding decisions, while NVIDIA technologies provide the compute behind the applications. Read on to learn how healthcare teams are using AI to improve and speed patient care. Tuesday, Nov. 17, 8:00 a.m. PT 🔗 Proximie Helps Surgical Teams Spend Less Time on Logistics and More Time With Patients As AI advances healthcare, surgery is a high-stakes, highly regulated setting for its use — and one with significant opportunity for efficiency gains. Only about 10% of time spent in the operating room is clinical. The rest is devoted to scheduling, turnover and documentation. With the help of NVIDIA technology, Proximie is introducing AI into operating room (OR) logistics so that clinicians can focus on taking care of patients. A New Vantage Point Proximie is using NVIDIA Cosmos 3 , the frontier open world foundation model family for physical AI, to power a platform used in more than 700 ORs today. Trained on a decade of data, it captures real-time audio, video and device signals from a close-up view of the surgery as well as a wide view of the whole room. The comprehensive view offers context held by no single person in the room, whether the surgeon, scrub nurse or coordinator. Agentic notifications and voice AI tools can call the next patient when a room is ready, document alerts and capture practitioner notes
